ai.description: This slender snake reaches 40–50 cm. It is brown with a distinct yellow vertebral stripe and dark lateral blotches. A V-shaped marking on the nape and enlarged, blade-like rear teeth are diagnostic.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Oligodon woodmasoni* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous yellow vertebral stripe running down the center of its back, which is absent in similar Indian kukri snakes.
ai.habitat: *Oligodon woodmasoni* inhabits the moist evergreen and semi-evergreen forests of the Andaman Islands, typically found in dense tropical vegetation at low elevations.
ai.behavior: The Yellow-striped Kukri Snake is primarily nocturnal and utilizes its specialized, blade-like teeth to slice into reptile eggs, its primary food source.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Oligodon woodmasoni* is oviparous, laying small clutches of eggs. While specific breeding data is limited, they are believed to reproduce during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Oligodon woodmasoni* is endemic to the Andaman Islands, where it inhabits low-to-mid elevation tropical forests within this unique biogeographic archipelago.
